headline: Medium pairwise risk: Airbyte can egress business data while awesome-nlp has no egress, creating leakage and downstream trust risks if outputs are chained.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem, or clipboard bridge is documented between airbyte and awesome-nlp. Airbyte exposes an API and broad network egress, but awesome-nlp has no I/O surfaces or runnable integration shown, so a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later connects Airbyte outputs into awesome-nlp prompts or files, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pipe Airbyte text directly into NLP prompts.
Add provenance labels to any transferred text.
requires-engineering: introduce content sanitization before any future handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, while awesome-nlp is documented with no network egress and no data classes touched. With no shared workspace or authenticated principal shown, direct leakage between the pair is not evidenced; the main risk is operator-mediated transfer of business data into text workflows.
conditions: IF both agents are later given the same shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF business data is copied from Airbyte into awesome-nlp inputs, that data may appear in downstream outputs.
mitigations: Keep business data out of NLP inputs.
Use separate service accounts.
Disable any shared folder mounts.
Review logs for copied payloads.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on handoff paths.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and API access, but awesome-nlp shows no write, network, or mutable-resource capabilities. There is no overlapping write surface, OAuth scope, or shared mutable resource documented, so capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp is later wrapped with write access to the same resources as Airbyte, conflict risk would need reassessment.
mitigations: Keep resource ownership separate.
Avoid granting shared write credentials.
Use read-only integration where possible.
Document any future shared mutable targets.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce business-data outputs, and awesome-nlp is a text/NLP repository that could be used to transform or summarize those outputs. However, no default action-taking authority or direct pipeline is documented, so cascading error requires an added orchestration step rather than arising inherently from the pair.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are treated as authoritative inputs to an NLP summarizer without verification, errors can propagate.
IF a downstream system acts on the NLP output, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Insert a human review step.
Require schema validation on Airbyte outputs.
Mark NLP output as untrusted.
Compare against source records before action.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, while awesome-nlp shows no data classes touched and no residency or retention commitments. The pair does not document a specific residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to uncertain handling of business data if it is routed into the NLP side.
conditions: IF regulated business data is routed from Airbyte into awesome-nlp, compliance review is required.
IF retention or logging differs across the two systems, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Classify data before transfer.
Avoid sending regulated data to the NLP side.
Check retention settings on both systems.
Record the legal basis for any transfer.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing.
